title: Notification architecture
description: Project: Notification architecture. Build and understand this project with step-by-step guidance.

data.text: Notification architecture extends real-time messaging to mobile push, email, and in-app banners. The challenge is not delivering a single notification; it is delivering the right notification to the right device, deduplicating across channels, and respecting user preferences without overwhelming them. Senior engineers treat notifications as a product feature with strict rate limits and measurable engagement metrics.

items: Separate notification creation from notification delivery to allow retry and fan-out
Use a notification worker that listens to a message bus and applies user preferences and rate limits
Support multiple channels: in-app, WebSocket push, mobile push (APNs, FCM), and email
Deduplicate notifications across channels so a user does not receive both an in-app banner and an email for the same event
Implement per-user and per-channel rate limits to prevent notification fatigue
Store notification preferences per channel per user: quiet hours, muted conversations, and importance thresholds
Design the data model to support both transactional notifications and aggregate digests

terms.definition: Sending a single event to multiple delivery channels or recipients, often implemented as a publish-subscribe pattern.
An external service such as Apple Push Notification service or Firebase Cloud Messaging that delivers notifications to mobile devices.
A user-defined time window during which non-critical notifications are suppressed or batched.
The diminished response to notifications caused by excessive volume, leading users to disable or ignore all notifications.
A batched summary of multiple notifications delivered as a single message at a scheduled interval.

data.text: Notifications are the primary retention lever for communication platforms. If users disable notifications because they are noisy or irrelevant, engagement drops and the product loses its real-time advantage. A senior engineer designs the notification system with user preference, channel capability, and rate limiting as first-class concerns.

data.title: Respect user attention
data.text: Always provide a way to mute or unsubscribe. Rate-limit notifications to a maximum of ten per user per hour for non-critical events. For critical alerts such as security or billing, bypass the rate limit but still allow users to opt out.

items: Event occurs: message received, mention, or system alert
Notification service creates a notification record with event type, recipients, and payload
Worker loads user preferences for each recipient: enabled channels, quiet hours, importance threshold
Worker filters recipients who should not receive this notification based on preferences
Worker applies rate limiting: if the user has exceeded the channel limit, defer to digest
Worker delivers via the highest-priority enabled channel: in-app if online, mobile push if app installed, email as fallback
Worker records delivery status and increments the user notification counter

data.title: Design a notification worker
data.description: Design a worker that receives events from a message bus and delivers notifications according to user preferences and rate limits. The worker should support in-app, mobile push, and email channels.
steps: Define the notification schema: eventType, recipientId, channel, payload, priority, and createdAt
Implement a preference loader that returns enabled channels and quiet hours for a user
Implement a rate limiter using a Redis sorted set per user per channel
Implement channel delivery adapters: WebSocket for in-app, FCM/APNs for mobile, SMTP or SES for email
Implement a digest queue that batches non-critical notifications for hourly delivery
Write a delivery log that records success, failure, and reason for each attempt
data.expectedOutcome: You should have a worker that respects user preferences, avoids notification fatigue, and provides clear delivery observability.

items.question: How do I handle mobile push token rotation?
items.answer: Store the latest token per user per device. On each delivery attempt, if the provider returns NotRegistered or InvalidRegistration, remove the token and prompt the user to re-enable notifications.

items.question: What if FCM is down?
items.answer: FCM is highly available, but you should still implement a fallback: queue the notification for retry and deliver via email or in-app when the user opens the app. Do not block the worker waiting for FCM.

items.question: Should I persist every notification?
items.answer: Yes. Persist notifications so users can view their notification history and so you can deduplicate across retries. Use the notification ID as the idempotency key.

data.title: Summary
points: Decouple notification creation from delivery with a worker and message bus
Respect user preferences and rate limits on every delivery
Use mobile push for critical real-time alerts and email for digests
Persist notifications for history, deduplication, and analytics
data.takeaway: Notifications are a product feature, not an infrastructure afterthought. The best notification systems are quiet by default and loud only when truly necessary.
